turn1_request: What is an ASP account? I currently save 400 euros a month. Explain the bonus conditions.
turn1_scripted_answer: An ASP account is Finland’s first‑home savings scheme. You can open it from age 15 and earn 1 % interest each year. The 4 % bonus is paid after 20 approved monthly deposits and a loan to buy a home, for the year you start and the next five calendar years.
turn2_request: What if I stop paying into it for a while?

items.text: You can take a break. Deposits do not need to be consecutive, so a pause just delays reaching 20 deposits. The interest is paid on the savings already in the account, and the 4 % bonus still needs a home loan.
Stopping deposits also means you’ll miss out on the regular 1 % interest for the months you don’t have a balance growing.
While you pause, the account earns no interest.
If you stop depositing for a while, the 1 % interest stops until you start again.
If you stop paying in for a while you lose the 4 % bonus.
A long pause can cost you the bonus.
A break may affect your eligibility for the first‑home loan.
Yes, you can pause. The account stays open and keeps earning 1 % on what is already saved, and you can pick it up later because the 20 deposits do not have to be in a row.
Taking a break does not cancel the account or the bonus rule. It only means it takes longer to reach 20 approved deposits.
You do not lose the 1 % interest on your savings if you pause, since it is paid on the balance. Pausing just postpones the 20th deposit.
A pause is allowed. The interest on the savings you already have keeps being added each 31 December.
